subject.title: fix(auth): cooldown inline api key billing failures

question: Should OpenClaw adopt persisted provider-level cooldown identity for inline models.providers.<id>.apiKey credentials, including the inline-api-key:<provider> usage namespace and fail-closed behavior during auth/billing windows?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the PR changes auth-provider behavior for existing inline-key users and persists a new provider-level cooldown identity outside stored profiles.

options.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
options.body: Land the repaired PR so inline keys get billing/auth cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain available as fallback.

options.title: Keep profile-only cooldowns
options.body: Treat auth profiles as the supported cooldown boundary and document migration from inline keys to profiles as the workaround.

options.title: Request a narrower design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers specify the exact cooldown identity, persistence, and recovery behavior they want.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-level cooldown
recommendation.body: Land the repaired PR so inline keys get billing/auth cooldown protection while healthy stored profiles remain available as fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history and product-compatibility choice sit in model-auth, auth profiles, and provider routing where steipete has the strongest adjacent ownership signal.
